title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 764-766 of the Longue Marche continuation). Grothendieck has just proved that the group Pi = <rho~, sigma~ | rho~^3 = sigma~^2> maps isomorphically onto SL(2,Z)~. Pi is B_3, the universal central extension of PSL(2,Z), with omega_0 = rho~^3 = sigma~^2 central. The proof uses the five lemma on the extension Z -> Pi -> SL(2,Z)/±1. His Corollary 1 (28) gives a presentation of GL(2,Z)~ = Pi ⋊ Z/2 with generators rho~, sigma~, tau~'. The relations are tau~'^2 = 1, rho~^3 = sigma~^2, and tau~' inverts both rho~ and sigma~. On this page he wants to rewrite this presentation with three involutive generators lifting the classical reflections of GL(2,Z).

(29) The three reflections downstairs are
- r_inf = diag(-1,1);
- r_0 = the swap matrix [[0,1],[1,0]];
- r_1 = [[-1,1],[0,1]].
All have determinant -1 and square to 1. One checks that r_0 r_1 = [[0,1],[-1,1]] has order 6, hence order 3 in PGL. Also r_inf r_0 = [[0,-1],[1,0]] has order 4, hence order 2 in PGL. This is the standard picture of PGL(2,Z) as the extended (2,3,∞) triangle (Coxeter) group.

(30) Relations downstairs: r_0 inverts rho and sigma, r_1 = rho^{-1} r_0 = r_0 rho, and r_inf = sigma r_0 = r_0 sigma^{-1}.

Upstairs, rho~ and sigma~ have infinite order. Hence:
- <rho~, tau~'> = D_rho~ ≅ D_∞;
- <sigma~, tau~'> = D_sigma~ ≅ D_∞;
- <omega_0, tau~'> = D_omega0 ≅ D_∞.
There are two inclusions, i: omega_0 -> rho~^3 (index 3) and j: omega_0 -> sigma~^2 (index 2), both fixing tau~'.

Corollary 1 then reads (32): GL(2,Z)~ ≅ D_∞ *_{D_∞} D_∞. This is the lift of the classical amalgam GL(2,Z) ≅ D_6 *_{D_2} D_4 (orders 12, 4, 8), equivalently PGL(2,Z) ≅ D_3 *_{Z/2×Z/2} D_2. It is consistent with B_3 = Z *_Z Z, since tau~' inverts omega_0 compatibly.

(33) In each dihedral factor he picks involutive generators:
- r~_0 = tau~' and r~_1 := rho~^{-1} r~_0 = r~_0 rho~ in D_rho~;
- r~_0 again (the line is left as dots) and r~_inf := r~_0 sigma~^{-1} in D_sigma~.
This leads on the next page to Corollary 2: GL(2,Z)~ = <r~_0, r~_1, r~_inf | r~_i^2 = 1, (r~_0 r~_1)^3 = (r~_inf r~_0)^2>. It is a 'Coxeter-like' group in which the Coxeter relations (ab)^3 = 1 and (ca)^2 = 1 are replaced by the single braid-type relation (ab)^3 = (ca)^2, a central element.

Purpose: a combinatorial description of the 'real' or extended version of B_3 = π1 of the moduli of elliptic curves with a tangential structure. Complex conjugation acts as the involution. This feeds Grothendieck's study of the Galois / Teichmüller tower in genus 1.
errors: No mathematical error. The machine transcription is wrong where it says D_6, D_8, D_4: the image clearly reads D_∞ for all three dihedral groups, which is correct because rho~, sigma~ and omega_0 have infinite order in B_3.
The second line of (33) is left unfinished ('r~_ρ = ......'). It should presumably be r~_0 = tau~' again, the common involution in D_sigma~.

The relation in (34) on the next page is written '(..)^3 = (..)^2 = 1', which taken literally would collapse to the PGL version. The intended relation (from Corollary 1) is (r~_0 r~_1)^3 = (r~_inf r~_0)^2 (= omega_0), not = 1. This is a slip or ambiguity in notation.

ideas.what: Classical reflection generators of GL(2,Z) / PGL(2,Z) as the extended (2,3,∞) triangle group
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses SL(2,Z) / cartographic groups (the latter likely, but unsure)

ideas.what: GL(2,Z)~ = B_3 ⋊ Z/2 as an amalgam of infinite dihedral groups D_∞ *_{D_∞} D_∞ with index-3 and index-2 inclusions
ideas.modern_name: Bass–Serre amalgam decomposition of the extended braid group B_3 ⋊ Z/2 (extended mapping class group of a one-holed torus)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; Serre (Trees) for the SL2/PGL2 analogues

ideas.what: Presentation by three involutions with relation (r0 r1)^3 = (r_inf r0)^2 central
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of the extended braid group B_3^± / extended Artin-type group

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but routine combinatorial group theory: lifting the classical dihedral amalgam of GL(2,Z) to the central extension by Z. The result B_3 ⋊ Z/2 ≅ D_∞ *_{D_∞} D_∞ follows directly from B_3 = Z *_Z Z and is standard folklore.
